title: The retention class list, the added event codes, the link column types and the feature IDs of four requirements are in no source
source: Ownership Map v1 (P1 rwb-source-data: table interaction; operations POST and GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions); Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-INT-014, DF-INT-018, DF-INT-022 to DF-INT-029, LOV-LEDGER-EVENT, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-DIRECTION, LOV-SOURCE); legacy story RWB-E2-034 sections 3, 7, 8, 11, 12, 13 and 18
section: s3 Preconditions; s7 AC1, AC2; s8 BR4; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s13 Configuration and reference data; s18 Traceability
description: The legacy story named the retention class per event code, added two values to LOV-LEDGER-EVENT and typed the two cross-service links, and no source fixes four things this slice needs. First, the class list and the periods behind it are Compliance's under DL26 and are not published, so the value of every class except the assumed ILG-STD is unstated. Second, the two values the legacy story adds to LOV-LEDGER-EVENT, PARTNER_RESULT and OFFER, are the story's own addition and no reference-data version carries them. Third, the response status of an append whose event code has no class row is not stated; this story refuses it with 422 and writes nothing rather than defaulting. Fourth, the type and length of treatment_id and proceeds_id are stated only by the legacy migration and the legacy text says the values are references, so the assumed uuid columns and the varchar lengths of the holder and class fields are a ruling and not a source value. The feature IDs of REQ-ILG-006, REQ-ILG-007, REQ-ILG-008 and REQ-ILG-014 are also not in the sources read for this story: the legacy traceability table names FEAT-ILG-06 to FEAT-ILG-10 only, for REQ-ILG-009 to REQ-ILG-013.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-034 section 3 'every event code takes class ILG-STD (assumed)' (DL26); section 3 'LOV-LEDGER-EVENT holds the added values PARTNER_RESULT and OFFER (addition)'; section 13 'adds contact_key varchar(255), from_holder_ref varchar(60), to_holder_ref varchar(60), treatment_id uuid, proceeds_id uuid, retention_class varchar(10)'; section 8 BR5 and BR6; section 18 traceability rows REQ-ILG-009 to REQ-ILG-013 with FEAT-ILG-06 to FEAT-ILG-10; LDM v8 DF-INT-022 to DF-INT-029.
legacy_ref: RWB-E2-034 (section 3, AC1, AC2, BR4, BR6, section 11, section 13, section 18)
proposed: Publish the retention class list and its periods with a version in the reference data of DP-07, add PARTNER_RESULT and OFFER to LOV-LEDGER-EVENT in the same version, confirm the uuid type of the two link columns in the Logical Data Model, and name the four feature IDs in the Business Requirements Epic 2; until then the assumed ILG-STD, the uuid links and the 422 refusal of sections 7, 11 and 12.1 hold and each is recorded as an assumption.

title: The interaction ledger is published on two different operation paths
source: Ownership Map v1 (P1 rwb-source-data: POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions, GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions); RWB-P1-E1066-APP section 12.1 (POST /interactions); RWB-P1-E1068-APP section 12.1 (GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions); RWB-P2-E2034-CON section 12.2 (POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions)
section: s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.8 Contract fakes; s18 Traceability
description: The Ownership Map lists the ledger append of P1 as POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions and its read as GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions, and the consumer contract of this legacy key fakes the append on that case-scoped path. The writer story of the same service publishes POST /interactions, so one resource has two published addresses and a client can build against either. The owning service is P1 in every source, so the conflict is one of naming and not of ownership; this story publishes the case-scoped form, which carries the case check and the scope in the address, and adds no third path.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 P1 rows 'GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions' and 'POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions'; RWB-P1-E1066-APP section 12.1 row POST /interactions; RWB-P1-E1068-APP section 12.1 row GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions; RWB-P2-E2034-CON section 12.2 row POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions; legacy RWB-E2-034 section 12 'GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions'.
proposed: Settle one path family for the ledger in RWB-P1-E1066-CON, realign the append row of RWB-P1-E1066-APP and its fake to the case-scoped form, and keep the case in the address so that the case check and the scope are part of it; until then the Ownership Map rows and section 12.1 of this story are the published ones.

title: The EFS outcome read and the contact-fact read that the channel consumer calls are named by interface only, with no path, parameter or owning story
source: RWB-P2-E2034-CON section 12.2 (the two P1 reads it calls); legacy story RWB-E2-034 sections 4, 12 and 13; RWB-P1-E2001-APP section 12.1 (GET /efs-history); Ownership Map v1 P1 operations
section: s3 Preconditions; s11 Data (legacy read fields); s19 Out of scope
description: The consumer of this legacy key calls two reads of rwb-source-data: the EFS contact-outcome rows of a business date and the contact key behind an entry. In the legacy story both were in-process calls of published Java interfaces, EfsContactHistory.outcomesFor and ContactQuery.byKey, and the consumer contract names them only by those interfaces because no operation of the Ownership Map answers them. The EFS history read of RWB-P1-E2001-APP answers the first for the case hand-over, but no story or ownership row in the sources read for this Work Package answers the contact-fact read, and neither path, query parameter nor response field set is stated. This story stores the contact key the caller supplies and reads neither, so the gap sits with the siblings and not in the store.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-034 section 12 'List<EfsContactOutcome> EfsContactHistory.outcomesFor(LocalDate businessDate)' and 'Optional<ContactView> ContactQuery.byKey(String contactKey)'; section 4 step 4 reads v_ace_efs_action; section 13 'EfsContactOutcomeReader'; RWB-P2-E2034-CON section 12.2 rows 'The EFS contact-outcome read of the rwb-source-data contract' and 'The contact-fact read of the rwb-source-data contract'; RWB-P1-E2001-APP section 12.1 confirms GET /efs-history only.
proposed: Publish the contact-fact read on the P1 base with its path, its contact-key parameter and its masked members, confirm that the EFS outcome read is the GET /efs-history operation of RWB-P1-E2001-APP or name the operation that answers the outcome list, and realign the two consumed rows of RWB-P2-E2034-CON to them.
